body:
## Groq — no first-party quota surface (evidence)

Implemented in the `opencode quota` subcommand (fork PR, provider `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/groq.ts`). Finding: **Groq exposes no first-party usage/quota endpoint an API key can read.**

Evidence gathered 2026-11-05:

- Groq's public API surface under `api.groq.com/openai/v1` is the OpenAI-compatible inference API (`/models`, `/chat/completions`, …). There is no `/usage`, `/billing`, `/subscription`, or organization-usage route; the docs' Rate Limits page (console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits) describes limits as enforced per model/organization and surfaced only:
  - as `x-ratelimit-*` response headers on inference calls (e.g. `x-ratelimit-limit-requests`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests`, `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens`, `x-ratelimit-reset-requests`, `x-ratelimit-reset-tokens`), and
  - on the authenticated web console's Limits page (console session, not the API key).
- A live probe with the stored Groq credential — `GET https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models` — succeeds (key valid) and returns **no** `x-ratelimit-*` headers on this route, so not even the header channel yields quota state without spending an inference call.

Behavior in the subcommand: the groq provider probes `/models` and maps any `x-ratelimit-*` headers present into windows; when none are present it returns `configured: true, ok: false` with `errorKind`/`failureClass` **`no-quota-surface`** and an explanatory error — never fabricated numbers. If Groq ships a usage endpoint later, this is the provider to extend.

## E2E proof — quota single-source is LIVE (2026-11-05 ~04:05 CST)

**(i) `opencode quota` covers every pool.** Fork PRs: [#1722](https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1722) (provider quota functions + subcommand, merged `13ab3dc5`) + [#1728](https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1728) (type cleanup, merged `255fa099`). Live default run: 14 results — antigravity, cline-pass, codex ×2, command-code, deepseek, mistral, opencode-go ×2, opendesign, openai.main, openai.alternate, turso ok; claude error (Anthropic 429, the provider's real state tonight); groq explicit `no-quota-surface` (evidence comment below). Mistral carries BOTH console budgets as dollar windows (trajectory across the night's heavy use: API $0.47→$0.84→$1.34→$1.81→~$2.04 of $15; Vibe $0.04→$0.68 of $150; reset 2026-12-01) — matching the admin-console truth in shape and magnitude at every read. Named asks fetch route-disabled pools (meta, command-code) by name, bypassing the disabled filter, per contract.

**(ii) quota-current.json is regenerated SOLELY from the subcommand.** Gatherer rewire merged: [#6136](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/6136) + [#6190](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/6190) (neutral cwd) + [#6191](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/6191) (OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH default). Retired: the in-process OpenChamber module import, gatherer-side Turso read, ClinePass adapter fill, file-export family. The production unit's final tick (journal in the proof bundle): `providers=14 ok=12`, file source = **opencode-quota**, duration 46s. Deployment note: until the nix switch ships the new system opencode binary, the unit's drop-in points QUOTA_SUBCOMMAND at the fork-built binary (`~/git/opencode-builds/quota-13ab3dc5/bin/opencode`) — remove the drop-in at the switch. One honest root-cause note: the first three production ticks failed on an UNQUOTED multi-word `Environment=` value in the hand-written drop-in (systemd split it, so the tick ran bare `opencode` with no args); the fail-soft contract held every time (previous file stood, heartbeat carried the error). The cwd/config-path changes are retained hardening — both effects were independently reproduced under systemd.

**(iii) Supabase lands on the same tick.** The gatherer's new sink writes one `agent.quota_records` row per pool entry per tick, source `opencode-quota` (verified in muse-dev2: fresh rows for every pool at each tick tonight). This replaces the `pm-pool` writer, which I found DEAD since 2026-10-29 (12 rows ever) — the "recorder is running" assumption in earlier passes was wrong; it is running now, from the single source.

**(iv) Dashboard.** [#6141](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/6141) merged: refresh button on the quota surface (POST /api/quota/refresh → manual gatherer trigger; polls until generatedAt advances; honest failure states; verified live, generatedAt advanced on click) and the `-direct` display rule as a pure function over the rendered set (10 tests; live page renders `antigravity.gemini` etc., ids unchanged). Post-tick /api/quota.json shows the mistral pool healthy with both budget windows, freshness source `opencode-quota`.

**Remaining open items (tracked, not silent):**
- opencode#1729 — subcommand hardening: 30s per-provider cap too tight for mistral's CDP read under listing concurrency (the gatherer carries documented explicit-ask workarounds for mistral + deepseek meanwhile), the listing currently omits deepseek though the named ask resolves it, and default config discovery without OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH is minutes-slow.
- vibe-direct's OWN provider quota function: the requirement + acceptance sit on opencode#1709 with the vibe lane. Tonight the Vibe budget figures flow through the mistral provider's console read (same account/endpoint); the subcommand-verified figures above are the acceptance numbers the vibe lane must match.
- Meta %: the provider implementation faithfully reports the portal read's no-data state (window exhausted server-side until 2026-11-09; key endpoint retired). No percentage exists to report right now; #6079's portal design is implemented provider-side and will surface a % when Meta's surface yields one.
- Out-of-scope service docs (named for the record): the aggregator also displays Supabase-platform and Cloudflare usage from their own export latest.json files — those are infrastructure-service usage documents, not provider quota, and were left as-is.

Proof bundle: ~/workspace/scratch/quota-single-source-2026-11-05/ (subcommand outputs, tick logs, final quota-current.json, dashboard verification).
